claims.text: A machine-learning model using chemical-disorder and lattice-dynamics descriptors can predict low phonon thermal conductivity in single-phase high-entropy alloys more accurately than conventional DFT or rule-of-mixtures methods.
FeCoCrMnNi is a chemically disordered high-entropy alloy representative of the proposed target materials.
The target alloys are single-phase materials.
These high-entropy alloys are used for thermal-insulation applications.
The proposed model will screen alloy compositions using computed disorder descriptors and simulated phonon characteristics.
Phonon heat transport dominates in the target alloys from ambient to moderately elevated temperatures.
Chemical disorder in high-entropy alloys produces local mass and force-constant fluctuations.
Mass and force-constant fluctuations enhance phonon scattering and reduce phonon lifetimes.
Strong chemical disorder disrupts phonon propagation and severely attenuates acoustic phonons in high-entropy alloys.
Disorder-induced phonon scattering and shortened phonon lifetimes lead to low lattice thermal conductivity.
Encoding disorder-induced phonon effects as model descriptors will make predictions more robust.
Compositions selected by the model will exhibit significantly lower lattice thermal conductivity when synthesized.
The selected compositions' low lattice thermal conductivity will result from increased disorder-induced phonon scattering.
Conventional DFT phonon calculations and rule-of-mixtures predictions do not fully account for disorder-driven phonon scattering.
The approach is primarily applicable to single-phase chemically disordered high-entropy alloys containing no more than five constituent elements.
The model's accuracy will degrade in multiphase or structurally complex alloys because additional mechanisms dominate thermal transport.
Experimental phonon data are limited across high-entropy-alloy composition space, and disorder effects are difficult to parameterize.
Inelastic neutron and X-ray scattering can be used to experimentally investigate phonon dynamics in FeCoCrMnNi.
